title: Deal-shape-stakeholder-momentum-play (v1)
content:
Purpose: quick, tactical play sellers use to build multi-stakeholder momentum and structure low-risk pilots that convert to reserved capacity deals.

Context / Why this exists:
- We repeatedly see deals stall because technical champions are excited but other stakeholders (security, infra, procurement, product) lack momentum or clear success metrics.
- This play focuses on 'deal shaping' — proactively aligning 3–4 stakeholder personas with a compact pilot that reduces procurement friction and demonstrates measurable value in 30 days.

One-page play summary (for SE / AE to memorize)
- Outcome we sell: "30-day pilot that proves throughput + cost predictability + policy controls"
- Required stakeholders: Integration engineer (champion), Platform/Infra owner, Security/compliance reviewer, Product/PO sponsor
- Minimum deliverables: demo script, data access checklist, SLO baseline, pilot evaluation rubric, fallback plan
- Hook: present expected 30-day ops delta (tokens/month, estimated unit cost, latency P50/P95) vs current baseline

High-level steps (operational)
1) Pre-call prep (AE + SE, 30m): map stakeholders, draft 1-page success criteria, assign owner for each criterion.
2) Stakeholder-brief cadence (15m each): run 15m tailored brief with each stakeholder — 7m to surface top risk, 8m to show how pilot mitigates
3) Pilot kickoff (2-week config + 30-day run): quick start template + weekly syncs
4) Mid-pilot check (day 15): show early telemetry + adjust routes/quantization if cost/latency off
5) Wrap + conversion: 2-hour review with exec summary + recommended reserved capacity commitment

Playbook mechanics / scripts (copy/paste bits)
- 15m security brief opener: "We will not onboard production data. Pilot will run in a sandbox VPC, KMS-managed keys, and we will provide a short audit log that includes request IDs and model version tags. Expected shared artifact: one-page security checklist (we finish it together)."
- Platform brief opener: "Our autopilot routing can run on dedicated pools to meet throughput targets; for the pilot we propose a single dedicated pool with capped burst to limit spend. We'll instrument cost-per-generation and provide token-level traces nightly."
- Product PO opener: "Success for the pilot is defined as an X% increase in task completion (or reduction in manual review) at a target latency. We will instrument sample prompts and A/B with/without caching to estimate steady-state cost."

Pilot skeleton (30-day) — minimal viable pilot
- Day 0–2: scope + signoffs on success rubric + create test dataset (50–200 sample cases)
- Day 3–10: infra setup (sandbox VPC or hosted tenant), model variant selection, prompt engineering pass, baseline run
- Day 11–25: live run on sample traffic, weekly telemetry digest (latency, cost, errors, quality metrics)
- Day 26–30: consolidate metrics, run quality regressions against golden prompts, present findings and recommended next steps

Success rubric (example)
- Latency: P50 < 150ms, P95 < 400ms on target payload (state target explicitly)
- Cost: per-1k-token cost vs baseline <= 60% of current external provider or internal cohort (adjustable)
- Quality: acceptance rate >= 85% on curated evaluation set (binary accept/reject by PO)
- Reliability: <1% error rate, graceful fallback on timeouts to smaller model variant

Objection handling (short snippets)
- "We can’t expose data" -> "Start with synthetic/anonymized samples + VPC/private deployment option; KMS + HSM integration available if needed; include explicit data handling clause in pilot MOU."
- "Cost sounds high" -> "We’ll run a 7–day baseline to surface per-token economics with/without caching and propose quantization profiles that typically reduce unit cost 20–60%. Also cap burst on dedicated pool."
- "What if quality regresses on our prompts?" -> "We’ll run paired regression tests on each rollout and pin model versions; rollback policy and A/B gating in the console."

Materials to prepare (attachments to share during qualification)
- One-page pilot MOU template (legal-lite)
- 15m stakeholder one-pager per persona (security, infra, product, procurement)
- Baseline telemetry checklist (what we need to measure day 0)
- Demo script with 5 live prompts and expected outputs (for SE to run)

Operational checklists (SE playbook)
- Pre-call checklist: confirm sample dataset, stake map, calendar invites to 15m briefs, draft MOU
- Kickoff checklist: tenant/provisioning details, KMS key name, whitelist IPs, team Slack channel created, alerting hooks set
- Mid-pilot checklist: nightly telemetry email configured, regression test run, cost triggers set at 70% of pilot budget

Conversion nudges (from pilot -> reserved capacity)
- Show model unit economics with projected monthly tokens at 2x and 5x scale (spreadsheet excerpt)
- Recommend 3-tier reserved commit options with rollback window + probation month
- Offer an ops runway: 2 weeks of free dedicated tuning + first-month discounted overage rate

Evidence kit (what to bring to the decision meeting)
- Executive one-pager: pilot goal, outcome metrics, recommended reserve level, top risks + mitigations
- Telemetry dashboard screenshots: latency distribution, cost trend, error rate, top N failing prompts with examples
- Live regression demo: 3 golden prompts run against the production candidate + fallback variant

Open questions / TODOs (working list)
- [ ] finalize MOU legal wording for sandbox-only data usage (legal review ticket JIRA-8234)
- [ ] quick spreadsheet template for AE to plug in estimated tokens and compute per-token economics (owner: Marco)
- [ ] SLAs to offer for a 30-day pilot (we currently only have SLA text at enterprise level)
- [ ] ask product for a small telemetry endpoint we can ship as a sample (Zoe)

Notes to self (rough, expect copy edits)
- Keep the stakeholder briefs to 15m — sellers consistently overrun and lose momentum.
- Emphasize "pilot is reversible" language — procurement likes soft exits.
- Make the MOU a one-pager; legal will hate it but it matters for procurement acceptance.

References / links included in artifacts:
- Confluence draft: deal-shaping templates (linked above)
- Example pilot telemetry export (internal dashboard sample)
- Slack thread: pilot-playbook-feedback (see linked_artifacts)

Quick copy for AE Subject lines (email templates)
- "30-day safe pilot to validate latency & cost for [use case] — quick 15m to align?"
- "Pilot MOU + one-pager: suggested success criteria for [company name]"

Appendix: short role cheat-sheets (one-liners to hand to SEs)
- Security reviewer: "Sandbox only, KMS keys, audit logs, limited sample data, legal-lite MOU."
- Platform owner: "Dedicated pool during pilot, capped burst, cost instrumentation nightly."
- Product PO: "We’ll measure quality on an agreed sample set and show delta vs current process."

Version history:
- v0.1 initial sketch (2024-11-12)

- v1.0 added legal pointers and conversion nudges (2025-01-21)
